caveats: League strength is an empirical transition weight (NCAA = 1.00 anchor), estimated from players who moved between leagues — it is evidence-based, not an official ranking.
Confidence and path counts are shown next to every weight; weights built on few direct transitions are weaker evidence.
Market lists show current draft-class prospects only (same quality filters as the Market view). A league page with few or zero market players says nothing about league strength.
A player appears on exactly one league page: the league where he has played the most minutes this season.

NCAA-to-league retention numbers are medians over real player transitions (paired seasons). Style and volume stats travel; shooting efficiency in a first season abroad is mostly noise — read the efficiency line as context, never as a projection.
Retention numbers are only shown for leagues with at least 15 observed NCAA transfers — below that the page says so instead of showing unstable numbers.
